n: The Lord addresses all who claim his name, warning that his anger burns against the rebellious, who will feel his power in the coming day of judgment.

f.g: A time when God comes to judge or bless.

n: Anyone unwilling to take up the cross, follow Christ, and keep his commandments will not be saved. Discipleship involves sacrifice.

f.w: take up his cross and follow me

n: When the Lord commands and the command is broken, the disobedient will be cut off in his timing.
The Lord can command and revoke as he sees fit; responsibility for revoked blessings rests on the rebellious. God adjusts his instructions in response to human choices.
Because Ezra Thayre wouldn’t leave, the Lord revokes the pairing of Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra and sends Thomas with Selah J. Griffin instead.

f.w: Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre

n: The earlier pairing of Selah J. Griffin and Newel Knight is also revoked because of the stubbornness of the Saints in Thompson.
Newel Knight is to stay and lead to Missouri any who are humble and willing.

f.w: the land which I have appointed

n: Ezra Thayre must repent of pride and selfishness and obey earlier instructions about the land where he lived—apparently a property dispute connected with Joseph Smith Sr.’s farm in Kirtland.

f.w: the place upon which he lives
f.g: A farm near Kirtland in which Ezra had invested money.

n: If he obeys—and the land is not divided—he may still go to Missouri.
Otherwise, he will get his money back, leave the land, and be removed from the Church.

f.g: Hosts = armies; the Lord as commander of heaven’s armies.

n: Though heaven and earth pass away, the Lord’s words will be fulfilled.

f.w: though the heaven and the earth pass away, these words shall not pass away

n: If Joseph Smith must refund Ezra’s money, the Lord will repay Joseph in Missouri, and those who give to him will be rewarded.
People will receive according to their deeds, even in lands of inheritance.

f.w: according to that which they do they shall receive

n: Turning to the Saints generally, the Lord says they have much to repent of; their sins remain unpardoned because they follow their own counsel rather than his.

f.w: you seek to counsel in your own ways

n: Their hearts are never satisfied; they disobey truth and take pleasure in wrongdoing.
Woe to the rich who refuse to share with the poor—their wealth will corrode their souls. In the judgment they will lament, in Jeremiah’s words, that the harvest is past and they are not saved.

f.g: Corrode or rust; eat away like a sore.

f.w: The harvest is past, the summer is ended

n: But woe also to the poor whose hearts are unbroken and greedy, who covet others’ goods and refuse to work. The Lord condemns attitudes, not economic status.

f.w: whose hands are not stayed from laying hold upon other men's goods
f.g: Who don’t hold back from grabbing other people’s things.

n: Blessed are the poor who are pure in heart, broken-hearted, and contrite; they will see God’s kingdom come in power to deliver them, and the earth’s riches will be theirs.

f.w: the poor who are pure in heart

n: The Lord will come with his reward, giving each person their due, and the poor will rejoice.

f.w: his recompense shall be with him

n: Their descendants will inherit the earth forever. The Lord ends his message.
